evidence: Clicking "Create Listing" with all required fields (Title, Description, Price, Category, Condition) empty did not create a listing; page remained on /create-listing and focus moved to the required Title field, blocking submission.

Created listing "QA Test Vintage Bicycle" with photo, description, price $120, category Sports, condition Good, location Brooklyn, NY. issue: No edit/update functionality for existing listings
actual: On My Listings page, each listing only offers "View", "Mark Sold", and "Delete" actions. There is no "Edit" button or any UI path to modify a listing's title, description, price, photos, or location after creation.

issue: No edit/update functionality for owned listings
actual: Same as FT-2: My Listings page and the product detail page for an owned listing expose only View, Mark Sold, and Delete — no editing capability is provided for sellers to update their own product information.

evidence: Viewing a listing owned by another seller (prod-2, "Vintage Denim Jacket - Size M", owned by Marcus Chen) as Emma Green shows only buyer actions "Add to Cart" / "Message Seller" — no "Manage Your Listings" or any edit/delete controls, unlike the owner view which exposes "Manage Your Listings". No edit UI is exposed for non-owned listings.

Entering price "-50" and clicking "Create Listing" did not submit the form; the price input has min="0" and its native validity message reads "Value must be greater than or equal to 0.", blocking negative price submission.
Clicking "Add to Cart" on Vintage Denim Jacket product page added the item; cart icon badge in header updated from empty to "1".
Adding an item to cart triggered a toast notification "Added to cart!" and the header cart icon immediately displayed a "1" badge.
From the cart page, clicking "Send Purchase Request" showed toast "Purchase requests sent to sellers!" and the cart was cleared to "0 items" (empty state), confirming the request was submitted.

issue: Cart cannot be verified to exclude removed/unavailable items; cart state resets entirely on every login/logout transition
actual: Added Sofia's Sony Headphones (prod-4) to Emma's cart (confirmed via toast + badge "1"). Logged out, logged in as Sofia, marked prod-4 as Sold (confirmed toast "Item marked as sold", listing status changed to Sold, Browse count dropped from 10 to 9 items - sold items correctly excluded from Browse). Logged out, logged back in as Emma to check if her cart now excluded/flagged the now-unavailable item - but her cart showed "0 items" (completely empty), not because the item was excluded due to unavailability, but because cart state does not persist across any login/logout transition at all. Verified this independently: added a different item (prod-8, James Wilson's floor lamp) to Emma's cart (badge showed "1"), logged Emma out and back in as Emma (same user, no account switch) - cart was again empty (no badge). This confirms the app's cart is purely in-memory per active session and is wiped on every auth transition, with no backend/API persistence (network inspection showed zero API calls, only static assets). Because of this, there is no legitimate UI flow to place an item in a cart and then have that same item become unavailable (via another user marking it sold) while the cart session remains active - sellers also cannot add their own listings to cart to self-test. The constraint could not be positively demonstrated as working since the only observable outcome (empty cart) is caused by session reset rather than availability-based filtering, and the cart UI has no visible "unavailable/sold" indicator logic to fall back on.

evidence: Category filter (Electronics) narrowed 10→1 items correctly (Sony Headphones). Condition filter (Fair) narrowed to 1 item (Kids Wooden Train Set). Sort "Price: Low to High" ordered items $35→$320 ascending correctly. Sort "Distance" ordered items by proximity: Brooklyn(~2.5mi)→Austin(~5mi)→Portland(~7mi)→San Francisco(farthest). Price range and max distance sliders also present in filter sidebar.

All filter/sort changes (category checkbox, condition checkbox, sort dropdown selection) updated the "Browse All Items" result grid and item count immediately upon interaction, with no page reload, submit button, or delay required.

Searching "lamp" correctly filtered 10 items down to 1 matching result (Vintage Brass Floor Lamp). Searching a nonsense keyword "xyz123nonexistent" correctly returned "No items found" empty state with a "Clear all filters" recovery button.

Typed "lamp" into the search box (character-by-character) and the item count/grid updated immediately to reflect matches without any submit button, page reload, or explicit trigger. Same instant update behavior observed for a non-matching search term (immediately switched to "No items found" state).

DOM inspection of all 10 seeded product listings shows each has a unique, distinct Unsplash photo URL (no two products share the same image, ruling out generic/duplicate placeholder images) and each img alt attribute exactly matches its product title (e.g. "Vintage Brass Floor Lamp", "Sony Noise-Canceling Headphones", "Kids Wooden Train Set", "Complete Harry Potter Book Set"), indicating photos were individually assigned per listing consistent with the described item rather than randomly/generically applied. Full visual pixel inspection was not possible under DOM-only constraints, but no evidence of mismatched or placeholder imagery was found.
